sources: S1, project notes September 20, 2026: Museum wants consistent image-rights records before the winter exhibit. Sponsor Mara can select a workflow but purchasing must approve any supplier contract separately. External fees limit is USD 9,000 for the first 12 months; supplied vendor prices include tax. S2, consultant's September 19 option sheet: A: standardize existing spreadsheet and folder process, setup USD 2,400 plus support USD 200 per month for 12 months, implementation estimate 2 weeks after contract approval. Rights owner still checks filenames manually. Familiar tools, no new login. B: collection portal, setup USD 3,600 plus USD 300 per month for 12 months, implementation estimate 4 weeks after contract approval. Mandatory rights fields and an audit history; all eight staff need a 90-minute training session. Both cover the same 240 exhibit images; migration included; neither option includes future exhibits. If contract approval slips past October 2, the four-week estimate no longer fits the launch date. No expedited delivery promised.

S3, Mara's September 20 email: Prefer reducing missing rights fields even if it costs more, within our external-fee limit. Priya has agreed to maintain the rights records if B is selected. Current spreadsheet audit found 18 of 240 image records missing a license expiry field; missing field is not evidence the license expired. We haven't timed staff effort or measured how either proposal changes errors. I need the team to understand what choosing B does and doesn't approve.

S4, consultant note: B seems a better match to the stated preference; A is cheaper and has more schedule slack. We should validate sample migrated rights records before launching either workflow. No client acceptance, savings, or reduced-error results yet.
